title: Build Resolver: Plan Dependency Resolution & Proposal

summary.goal: Add a build resolver service to Planner that takes an initiative_id or set of plan_ids, resolves inter-plan dependencies into a topologically-sorted tier structure, checks Forge for previous completions, and returns a BuildProposal for user review before execution.
in_scope: Inter-plan dependency resolution from plan metadata
Previous completion checking (queries Forge API for run history)
Auto-inclusion of missing dependencies with warnings
BuildProposal response with tiers, warnings, skipped plans, estimates

acceptance_criteria.description: POST /api/builds/propose accepts { initiative_id } or { plan_ids: [...] } and returns a BuildProposal
Resolver reads inter-plan dependencies and computes topological tiers
If plan B depends on plan A and only B is selected, A is auto-included with a warning
Circular dependencies are detected and returned as errors in the proposal
Plans with recent successful Forge runs are marked as 'already_completed' in the proposal
Plans that are still draft (not approved) are flagged with a warning
Proposal includes per-tier plan counts and total step counts for estimation
When initiative_id is provided, all plans under that initiative are included
Plans can have explicit depends_on_plans field linking to other plan_ids

observations: Inter-plan dependencies need to be stored somewhere queryable at runtime
Feature files have depends_on but those reference feature_ids not plan_ids
Plans already have a plan_id and belong to initiatives — need a depends_on_plans field on the plan entity
The resolver is stateless — it computes the proposal fresh each time from current data
Forge run history is queried via HTTP (GET /api/forge/runs?plan_id=X&status=completed)
The proposal is ephemeral — it's not stored. User reviews it, then submits to Forge.
questions: Should depends_on_plans be on the Plan entity or the PlanVersion?
How do we initially populate depends_on_plans for existing mull plans?

proposal_shape.BuildProposal: { tiers: ProposalTier[], warnings: ProposalWarning[], auto_included: string[], total_plans: number, total_steps: number }
proposal_shape.ProposalPlan: { plan_id: string, goal: string, steps_count: number, status: 'ready' | 'already_completed' | 'draft_warning', previous_run?: { run_id, status, completed_at } }

architect.dependency_source: Plan entity gets a depends_on_plans: string[] field. Populated during plan creation (from feature metadata) or manually. Stored in plans table as JSON.

steps.title: Add depends_on_plans column to plans table and update Plan entity
steps.description: Add a depends_on_plans TEXT column (JSON array of plan_ids) to the plans table via migration. Update the Plan Zod schema and factory functions to include the new field.

acceptance_criteria.description: Migration in storage/migration.ts: ALTER TABLE plans ADD COLUMN depends_on_plans TEXT DEFAULT '[]' — with PRAGMA table_info check for idempotency
PlanSchema in domain/plan.ts extended with: depends_on_plans: z.array(z.string().uuid()).default([])
createPlan() factory sets depends_on_plans: [] by default
rowToPlan() converter in storage/sqlite/converters.ts parses depends_on_plans from JSON string
planToRow() or INSERT statement serializes depends_on_plans via JSON.stringify()
updatePlan() supports updating depends_on_plans field
GET /api/plans/:id returns depends_on_plans in response

architecture.pattern: Same as existing migrations — PRAGMA table_info check, ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN. JSON column stored as TEXT, parsed in converter.

steps.title: Define BuildProposal domain types
steps.description: Create Zod schemas and TypeScript types for BuildProposal, ProposalTier, ProposalPlan, ProposalWarning, and the propose request schema.

acceptance_criteria.description: ProposalPlanSchema: z.object({ plan_id: z.string().uuid(), goal: z.string(), steps_count: z.number(), status: z.enum(['ready', 'already_completed', 'draft_warning']), previous_run: z.object({ run_id: z.string(), status: z.string(), completed_at: z.string() }).optional() })
ProposalTierSchema: z.object({ tier: z.number().int().nonnegative(), plans: z.array(ProposalPlanSchema) })
ProposalWarningSchema: z.object({ type: z.enum(['auto_included', 'draft_plan', 'circular_dependency', 'modified_since_last_run']), plan_id: z.string().uuid().optional(), message: z.string() })

BuildProposalSchema: z.object({ tiers: z.array(ProposalTierSchema), warnings: z.array(ProposalWarningSchema), auto_included: z.array(z.string().uuid()), total_plans: z.number(), total_steps: z.number() })

ProposeRequestSchema: z.object({ initiative_id: z.string().uuid().optional(), plan_ids: z.array(z.string().uuid()).optional() }).refine(data => data.initiative_id || (data.plan_ids && data.plan_ids.length > 0), { message: 'Either initiative_id or plan_ids required' })
All types exported: BuildProposal, ProposalTier, ProposalPlan, ProposalWarning, ProposeRequest

architecture.pattern: Zod-first with inferred types, same as plan.ts

steps.title: Implement topological sort and dependency resolution service
steps.description: Create a build-resolver service that resolves plan dependencies into topologically-sorted tiers. Handles auto-inclusion of missing dependencies, circular dependency detection, and draft plan warnings.

acceptance_criteria.description: resolveToTiers(plans: Plan[]): { tiers: Map<number, string[]>, warnings: ProposalWarning[], missingDeps: string[] } — Kahn's algorithm for topological sort

If plan B depends on plan A and A is not in the input Plan[] set, A's plan_id is added to missingDeps return array (propose() is responsible for fetching missing plans and re-calling resolveToTiers with the expanded set)
Circular dependency detection: if cycle found, returns warning { type: 'circular_dependency', message: 'Circular dependency detected involving plans: [ids]' } and places cycled plans in highest tier
Plans with no dependencies go in tier 0. Plans depending only on tier 0 plans go in tier 1. Etc.
Draft plans (latest version status='draft') flagged with warning { type: 'draft_plan', plan_id, message: 'Plan has no approved version' }

Pure function — takes Plan[] and returns tiers + warnings + missingDeps. No storage or HTTP calls. Auto-inclusion is driven by propose() which loops: resolve → fetch missing → resolve again until missingDeps is empty.

architecture.algorithm: Kahn's algorithm: 1. Build adjacency list from depends_on_plans. 2. Compute in-degree for each plan. 3. Initialize queue with in-degree=0 nodes (tier 0). 4. Process queue: remove node, decrement neighbors, add to next tier when in-degree=0. 5. If remaining nodes after algorithm, they're in cycles.

steps.title: Implement Forge run history client for completion checking
steps.description: Create a lightweight HTTP client that queries Forge for recent successful runs by plan_id. Used to mark plans as 'already_completed' in the proposal.

acceptance_criteria.description: ForgeClient class or function: { getRecentRuns(planId: string, status?: string): Promise<{ run_id, status, completed_at }[]> }
Calls GET /api/forge/runs?plan_id={planId}&status=completed&limit=1 on the configured Forge URL
ForgeClientConfig: { base_url: string, timeout_ms?: number }
Returns empty array on connection error or 404 (graceful degradation — missing Forge doesn't break proposals)
createForgeClient(config) factory function

architecture.pattern: Same pattern as forge-core's PlannerClient — lightweight fetch wrapper with Zod response validation. Since Planner and Forge are co-located in the same server, base_url is http://localhost:3001.

steps.title: Implement propose() orchestration function
steps.description: Create the main propose() function that orchestrates the full proposal workflow: resolve input to plans, compute tiers, check completions, assemble BuildProposal response.

acceptance_criteria.description: propose(input: ProposeRequest, deps: { storage: PlanStorage, forgeClient: ForgeClient }): Promise<BuildProposal>
If initiative_id: fetches all plans via storage.listPlans({ initiative_id })
If plan_ids: fetches each plan via storage.getPlan(id), throws 404 for missing

Calls resolveToTiers() in a loop: if missingDeps returned, fetches each from storage.getPlan(), adds auto_included warning, appends to plan set, re-resolves. Loop exits when missingDeps is empty (max 10 iterations to prevent runaway).
For each plan, queries forgeClient.getRecentRuns() — if recent completed run exists, marks plan as 'already_completed'
Assembles BuildProposal with tiers, warnings, auto_included ids, total_plans count, total_steps count (sum of steps across all plan versions)
Each ProposalPlan includes goal from latest version summary, steps_count from latest version

architecture.pattern: Orchestration function composing resolver + forge client. Forge completion checks run in parallel via Promise.all() for all plans.

steps.title: Add POST /api/builds/propose endpoint
steps.description: Create handler and route for the propose endpoint. Validates request, calls propose(), returns BuildProposal. Wire into planner router.

acceptance_criteria.description: Handler: validates body with ProposeRequestSchema.safeParse(), calls propose(), returns { proposal } with 200
400 if neither initiative_id nor plan_ids provided
404 if initiative_id doesn't exist or plan_ids reference missing plans
Route registered in planner router: POST /builds/propose

createRouter() signature extended: createRouter(storage: PlanStorage, opts?: { forgeClient?: ForgeClient }). ForgeClient created in server.ts with forgeUrl config. Build routes only registered when forgeClient is provided.
Works without Forge running — forgeClient returns empty results, proposal still computes tiers correctly without completion status

architecture.pattern: Same handler factory pattern as plans.ts handlers. ForgeClient optional dep — if not provided, all plans show as 'ready'. createRouter signature becomes createRouter(storage, opts?) to avoid breaking existing callers.
